name: Insulin with hypoglycemia or poor intake
message: Insulin from the Type 1 diabetes row can worsen hypoglycemia when the patient is already hypoglycemic, NPO, or has poor oral intake.
suggestedAction: Check current glucose and meal status; hold, reduce, or adjust insulin dose per protocol before administration.

name: Glipizide with hypoglycemia or poor intake
message: Glipizide from the Type 2 diabetes row can cause prolonged hypoglycemia, especially with low glucose, missed meals, NPO status, or poor intake.
suggestedAction: Avoid or hold glipizide until intake and glucose are stable; consider safer diabetes options for the current context.

name: Metformin during acute illness or renal risk
message: Metformin from the Type 2 diabetes row should be held in acute illness, AKI, hypoxia, sepsis, shock, dehydration, DKA, or metabolic acidosis because lactic acidosis risk may increase.
suggestedAction: Hold metformin and reassess renal function, perfusion, oxygenation, and acid-base status before restarting.

name: Semaglutide or sitagliptin with pancreatitis concern
message: Semaglutide or sitagliptin from the Type 2 diabetes row should be used cautiously when pancreatitis history or concerning abdominal pain is present.
suggestedAction: Avoid starting or temporarily hold and evaluate for pancreatitis if symptoms suggest it.

name: Sacubitril-valsartan with ACE/ARB angioedema or recent ACE inhibitor
message: Sacubitril-valsartan from the heart failure row should be avoided with prior ACE/ARB angioedema or if an ACE inhibitor was used within the last 36 hours.
suggestedAction: Do not administer; verify ACE inhibitor washout and angioedema history, then choose an alternative regimen if needed.

name: Beta blocker with asthma/COPD, heart block, or decompensated HF
message: Metoprolol or propranolol from the heart failure/hyperthyroid rows can worsen bronchospasm, bradycardia/heart block, shock, or decompensated heart failure.
suggestedAction: Review heart rate, blood pressure, conduction disease, respiratory status, and HF stability before giving a beta blocker.

name: Methimazole with fever, sore throat, or neutropenia
message: Methimazole from the hyperthyroid row can rarely cause agranulocytosis; fever, sore throat, infection symptoms, or neutropenia require urgent review.
suggestedAction: Hold methimazole and obtain CBC/ANC urgently; escalate for clinician review.

name: Thyroid hormone with recent MI or significant cardiac disease
message: Levothyroxine or liothyronine from the hypothyroid row should be used cautiously in recent MI, unstable angina, or significant cardiac disease because thyroid hormone can increase myocardial oxygen demand.
suggestedAction: Start low, titrate slowly, and verify cardiac stability before dose escalation.
